data.cultural_impact: The name Estelle has a rich cultural history, originating from the Hebrew language and meaning 'star.' It has been adopted and cherished throughout various cultures and time periods. In the Middle Ages, the name became popular in France, where it was often given to girls born on the feast day of St. Estrella, a Spanish saint. In the English-speaking world, the name gained further popularity during the 19th and 20th centuries. Estelle has a soft, melodic sound, making it a timeless and elegant choice for a girl's name.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Estelle has profound spiritual significance, rising from the biblical story of Esther. Esther, a Jewish woman chosen to become the queen of Persia, used her position to save her people from destruction. She displayed great courage and faith, risking her life to intervene on behalf of her people. Her story reminds us of the power of faith and the courage it takes to stand up for what is right. As a Christian name, Estelle carries the message of hope and belief, inspiring those who bear it to live their lives with faith and conviction.

historical_references.reference: Estelle, the daughter of King Louis XI of France, was born on 1453. She was named after the Saint Elisabeth of Hungary, who was known for her charitable works and holiness. Estelle grew up to become the Duchess of Brittany and played a significant role in the political intrigues of the Renaissance period in Europe.

historical_references.reference: Esther, a Jewish queen of Persia in the 5th century B.C., saved her people from destruction by Haman, an advisor to King Ahasuerus. Her name in Hebrew means 'star.' Some historians suggest that early Christians adopted the name Esther for girls in honor of this biblical queen, and the name Estelle is believed to be a variant of Esther.
